title: Turning Vague Requirements into Measurable NFR Budgets
objective: Take a realistic system brief and produce quantified, sourced budgets for at least four non-functional requirements.
whyThisMatters: Every later architecture decision in this curriculum is judged against a stated number. "Fast" and "reliable" cannot be designed against; a p99 latency target and an availability percentage can. An architect who cannot quantify a requirement cannot defend a design built against it.
evidence: An NFR sheet naming at least four distinct quality attributes, each with a quantified target and a stated source or assumption for that number
Git history showing the sheet was revised at least once, with a commit message or note stating what changed the number and why
A short note naming which NFR was hardest to quantify and how the final number was chosen
acceptanceCriteria: At least four distinct non-functional requirements are each stated as a measurable number, not an adjective.
Each budget names the source or reasoning used to arrive at that number (a benchmark, a comparable system, an explicit stated assumption).
The revision history shows at least one budget changed after the first draft, with a note stating why.
